task: Compute the sum of squares 1+4+9+...+100 by writing and evaluating lisp code; store the number in rlm state as answer. When the goal is achieved, evaluate (final true).
lesson: Today I learned rlm-set requires the answer key as the first argument.

nodes.code: (let ((sum 0)~~NL~~      (i 1))~~NL~~  (while (<= i 100)~~NL~~    (set! sum (+ sum (* i i)))~~NL~~    (set! i (+ i 1)))~~NL~~  (rlm-set answer sum)~~NL~~  (final true))
